newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius Fund posts higher 1996 interim profit.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius Fund posts higher 1996 interim profit.

text.p: Mauritius Fund posted higher interim profit of $204,320 for the half year ended 30 June 1996 from $134,273 in the corresponding period of 1995, the company said in an interim report published on Friday.
The Fund's six-month interim income for 1996 was lower at $519,941 from $577,314 in 1995 while net assets per share fell to $10.04 on 30 June 1996 from $11.27 at 31 December 1995.
Company officials blamed the Fund's decrease in net asset value to a depreciation of the Mauritian rupee versus the dollar and falling share prices on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius.

"A 6.7 percent fall in the Mauritius Stock Exchange index, coupled with a 9.6 percent decline in the value of the Mauritian rupee against the dollar, has resulted in the dollar net asset value falling by 10.9 percent during the six months to June 1996," Chairman John Heywood said in the interim report.
Mauritius Fund's investments in the stock exchange also went through a sectoral shift during the first half of 1996.
"The directors have decided to increase the Fund's exposure to the finance and tourism sectors as they appear likely to continue to offer better growth prospects," Heywood said.
Mauritius Fund's investments were valued at $24.45 million as at 30 June 1996, down from $27.64 million one year earlier.

The majority of the investments were made in stocks listed on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius, with Mauritius Commercial Bank, State Bank of Mauritius and conglomerate Rogers accounting for more than 30 percent of the Fund's total investments.
The Fund also holds shares quoted on the over-the-counter Market of the Mauritian bourse and the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange.
